subtitle: 2016 · 1.5 dCi 75 hp · K9K

card.intro: Fourth-generation Clio (2012–2019), 2016 model with the 75 hp 1.5 dCi turbodiesel. Click a component on the model or in the list to see what it does, its data, maintenance and replacement parts.
specs: Common rail, fixed-geometry turbo with intercooler
card.note: Approximate values: they may vary with trim level, homologation and production year.
card.credits: 3D body model: «Renault Clio MK4 2012-2020» by <author>Merc_TV on Sketchfab</author>, license <license>CC BY 4.0</license>. Engine bay, mechanicals and wheels are added reconstructions.

partNote: Approximate data for educational purposes for the Clio IV 1.5 dCi 75 (K9K 612/628). Intervals, quantities and part numbers change with year and version: always verify with the owner's manual or the VIN.

engine.name: K9K 1.5 dCi engine
engine.description: The heart of the car: an inline 4-cylinder turbodiesel mounted transversely. From bottom to top you can see the oil pan, the cast-iron block, the aluminum cylinder head with a single camshaft (8 valves) and the valve cover. It is one of the most widespread diesels in Europe (Renault, Dacia, Nissan, Mercedes).
engine.where: In the center of the engine bay, offset slightly to the right; the transmission is bolted to the left side.
maintenance: Oil and filter change: every 30,000 km or 2 years per the owner's manual; many mechanics recommend 15,000 km / 1 year to protect the bearings and turbo.
Check the oil level every 1,000–2,000 km.
Warm up the engine before driving hard, and let it idle for a few seconds before shutting it off after highway driving.
faults: Connecting-rod bearing wear (especially with overly long oil-change intervals): metallic knocking noise.
Leaks from the valve cover or the crankshaft oil seal.
Smoke and loss of power caused by a dirty EGR valve or injectors.
oem: 5W-30 RN0720 engine oil (e.g. Elf Solaris DPF)

engine-cover.name: Engine cover
engine-cover.description: Plastic cosmetic and sound-absorbing cover over the cylinder head, injectors and fuel rail. It comes off by pulling it straight up: it is held by press-fit rubber grommets. Hide it with the "Hide" button to see what's underneath.
engine-cover.where: On top of the engine; it's the first thing you see when you open the hood.
maintenance: No maintenance: just check that the mounting grommets are intact.

oil-filler-cap.name: Oil filler cap
oil-filler-cap.description: This is where you add engine oil. A light-colored "mayonnaise" under the cap may be condensation (short trips) or, in serious cases, coolant in the oil.
oil-filler-cap.where: On the valve cover, right side of the engine.
maintenance: Top up with the engine off and the car on level ground, a little at a time, checking with the dipstick.

oil-dipstick.name: Oil dipstick
oil-dipstick.description: Metal rod with a yellow handle for checking the oil level. Read the level with the engine off for at least 5–10 minutes and the car on level ground.
oil-dipstick.where: On the front side of the engine, toward the center.
maintenance: Pull it out, wipe it, push it fully back in and pull it out again: the level must be between the two marks.

oil-filter.name: Oil filter
oil-filter.description: Traps impurities in the oil. On this generation of the K9K it is a paper cartridge inside a plastic housing screwed onto the front of the engine block.
oil-filter.where: At the front of the block, low down; reachable from above or below.
maintenance: Replace at every oil change together with the housing O-rings.
Housing tightening torque: approx. 25 Nm (it is printed on the cap).

timing-belt.name: Timing belt
timing-belt.description: Under this cover is the toothed belt that synchronizes the crankshaft and camshaft and also drives the high-pressure pump. If it breaks, the valves hit the pistons: very serious damage.
timing-belt.where: Right side of the engine (passenger side), behind the plastic cover.
specs: Set with locking pins on the crankshaft and camshaft
maintenance: Complete kit replacement (belt + tensioner): approx. 150,000 km or 6 years — verify in the specific car's owner's manual.
Replace the water pump and accessory belt at the same time.
faults: Breakage due to missed replacement or a seized tensioner.
Whining or humming from the timing side = tensioner or water pump at end of life.

water-pump.name: Water pump
water-pump.description: Circulates coolant between the engine and radiator. It is driven by the timing belt, which is why it is replaced together with it.
water-pump.where: On the right side of the block, behind the timing cover.
maintenance: Replace together with the timing belt.
faults: Pink/green coolant leaks on the timing side.
Noisy bearing.

accessory-belt.name: Accessory drive belt (poly-V)
accessory-belt.description: Ribbed belt driven by the crankshaft pulley that turns the alternator and A/C compressor. An automatic tensioner keeps it tight.
accessory-belt.where: Right end of the engine, in front of the timing cover.
maintenance: Replace with the timing belt kit (or sooner if cracked).
Never let pieces of a broken accessory belt get into the timing drive: on the K9K this is a classic engine killer.
faults: Squealing when cold, fraying.
Crankshaft pulley (damper) with delaminated rubber.

alternator.name: Alternator
alternator.description: Converts part of the engine's power into electricity to charge the battery and power all electrical loads. On Stop&Start / Energy versions it is controlled by the ECU to recover energy when coasting.
alternator.where: At the front of the engine, upper right.
faults: Battery warning light on, lights dimming.
Noisy overrunning (freewheel) pulley.

ac-compressor.name: A/C compressor
ac-compressor.description: Compresses the air-conditioning refrigerant. It is driven by the accessory belt and engages through an electromagnetic clutch.
ac-compressor.where: At the front of the engine, lower right, below the alternator.
specs: R134a or R1234yf depending on production date (see the label under the hood)
maintenance: Run the A/C for a few minutes even in winter to lubricate the seals.
Recharge/check every 2–3 years.

ac-condenser.name: A/C condenser
ac-condenser.description: It's the air conditioning's "radiator": it cools the compressed refrigerant and turns it back into liquid. It is the first heat exchanger behind the bumper, so it is the most exposed to stones and bugs.
ac-condenser.where: In front of the engine radiator, right behind the grille.
faults: Punctures from road debris → refrigerant leak, A/C that doesn't cool.

radiator.name: Engine radiator
radiator.description: Aluminum heat exchanger that transfers heat from the coolant to the air. Hot coolant enters at the top and returns to the engine cooler from the bottom.
radiator.where: Behind the grille, between the condenser and the fan.
maintenance: Coolant replacement: approx. every 4–5 years (verify in the owner's manual).
Keep the fins clear of leaves and bugs.

radiator-fan.name: Radiator cooling fan
radiator-fan.description: Electric fan that pulls air through the radiator and condenser when the car is stopped or moving slowly, or when the A/C is on.
radiator-fan.where: Behind the radiator, toward the engine.
faults: Burned-out motor or failed resistor: overheating in traffic.

radiator-hoses.name: Radiator hoses
radiator-hoses.description: Rubber hoses connecting the engine and radiator. The upper one carries hot coolant to the radiator, the lower one returns it to the engine.
maintenance: Check that they aren't swollen, cracked or oily; check the clamps.

coolant-reservoir.name: Coolant reservoir
coolant-reservoir.description: Expansion tank of the cooling system. Check the level with the engine COLD; it must be between MIN and MAX. Never open the cap with the engine hot: the system is under pressure.
coolant-reservoir.where: At the back of the engine bay, right side, near the firewall.
faults: Dropping level = a leak (water pump, radiator, hoses) to be tracked down right away.

thermostat.name: Thermostat
thermostat.description: Valve that keeps the circuit to the radiator closed until the engine reaches operating temperature (approx. 83–89 °C), then opens it.
thermostat.where: On the cylinder head, right side, inside a plastic housing.
faults: Stuck open: engine doesn't warm up, high fuel consumption, weak cabin heat.
Leaking plastic housing.

fuel-filter.name: Diesel fuel filter
fuel-filter.description: Traps dirt and water in the diesel fuel before they reach the pump and injectors, which work to tolerances of thousandths of a millimeter. It has a water-in-fuel sensor and, next to it, the manual priming bulb.
fuel-filter.where: In the engine bay, front right side.
maintenance: Replacement: approx. every 60,000 km (every 2 services) or sooner with fuel of doubtful quality.
After replacement, bleed the air with the priming bulb until it becomes firm.
faults: Clogged filter: hesitation under acceleration, hard starting.
Water-in-fuel warning light.

high-pressure-pump.name: High-pressure fuel pump
high-pressure-pump.description: Raises the diesel fuel to approx. 1600 bar and sends it to the rail. It is driven by the timing belt and lubricated by the fuel itself: that's why you must never run out of fuel or put in gasoline by mistake.
high-pressure-pump.where: Right side of the engine, high up toward the firewall.
faults: Metal shavings in the system (worn pump) → injector damage.
Faulty pressure regulator: stalling, hard starting.

fuel-rail.name: Fuel rail (common rail)
fuel-rail.description: Steel accumulator tube that holds diesel fuel at very high pressure, ready for the 4 injectors: this is the "common rail". It carries a pressure sensor that the ECU reads continuously.
fuel-rail.where: On top of the cylinder head, rear side, under the engine cover.
faults: Failed rail pressure sensor: engine in limp mode.
Never loosen the lines with the engine running: 1600 bar jet.

injectors.name: Injectors
injectors.description: Four electronic injectors that atomize diesel fuel directly into the cylinders, with multiple injections per cycle (pilot, main, post). Each has a calibration code that must be programmed into the ECU when it is replaced.
injectors.where: On the cylinder head, one per cylinder, under the engine cover.
specs: Common-rail solenoid injectors (Continental/Siemens VDO on Euro 5)
Individual code to be entered with a diagnostic tool
faults: Leaking copper sealing washers: black tar around the injector and a "chuff-chuff" sound at idle.
Rough idle, smoke, knocking.

glow-plugs.name: Glow plugs
glow-plugs.description: Four heating elements that warm the combustion chambers to help cold starting (the yellow "coil" light on the instrument cluster). They stay on for a few moments after starting to reduce smoke and noise.
glow-plugs.where: Screwed into the cylinder head, front side, one per cylinder.
maintenance: Check/replace approx. every 100,000–120,000 km; remove them with the engine warm so they don't snap.
faults: Hard starting and white smoke when cold, check engine light.

fuel-tank.name: Fuel tank
fuel-tank.description: 45-liter plastic tank under the rear seat. Inside is the fuel level float; the filler neck runs from the fuel door on the right side.
fuel-tank.where: Under the floor, ahead of the rear axle.
specs: EN 590 diesel (max B7; B10 where permitted by the owner's manual)

fuel-flap.name: Fuel door
fuel-flap.description: Small door covering the fuel cap. It unlocks together with the central locking.

air-filter.name: Air filter box
air-filter.description: Holds the paper filter that cleans the air drawn in by the engine. A diesel draws in thousands of liters of air per minute: a dirty filter robs power and increases fuel consumption and smoke.
air-filter.where: Front left side of the engine bay.
maintenance: Replacement: approx. every 30,000 km or 2 years (halve the interval in dusty areas).

maf-sensor.name: MAF sensor (mass air flow meter)
maf-sensor.description: Hot-film sensor that measures how much air enters the engine. The ECU uses this data to meter fuel and EGR.
maf-sensor.where: On the duct at the outlet of the air filter box.
maintenance: It can be cleaned with a dedicated spray; never touch the sensing element.
faults: Sluggish engine, black smoke, high fuel consumption; often with no warning light on.

intake-duct.name: Turbo intake duct
intake-duct.description: Duct that carries filtered air from the filter box to the turbo compressor inlet. The engine's crankcase breather (oil vapor) also feeds into it, which is why a thin film of oil inside is normal.
faults: Cracks or loose clamps: unfiltered air entering the turbo.

turbocharger.name: Turbocharger
turbocharger.description: Exhaust gases spin a turbine (hot side, rusty) connected by a shaft to a compressor (cold side, aluminum) that forces more air into the cylinders. On the 75 hp version it is fixed-geometry with a wastegate controlled by a vacuum actuator. It spins at over 200,000 rpm, lubricated by engine oil.
turbocharger.where: Behind the engine, on the firewall side, attached to the exhaust manifold.
maintenance: Good oil changed often = a long-lasting turbo.
Don't shut the engine off immediately after hard driving.
faults: Loud whistling, blue smoke, large amounts of oil in the hoses.
Stuck wastegate: too little or too much boost.

intercooler-hoses.name: Intercooler hoses
intercooler-hoses.description: Reinforced rubber hoses that carry the (hot) compressed air from the turbo to the intercooler and from there (cooled) to the intake manifold.
maintenance: Check the clamps and look for oil traces on the outside.
faults: Split or disconnected hose: loud whooshing under acceleration, loss of power and black smoke.

intercooler.name: Intercooler
intercooler.description: Air-to-air radiator that cools the compressed air from the turbo: cooler air is denser, so more oxygen and better efficiency.
intercooler.where: At the front, lower left next to the radiator.
faults: Punctures or leaking end tanks.

intake-manifold.name: Intake manifold
intake-manifold.description: Distributes air (and recirculated EGR gases) to the 4 cylinders. Over the years it gets coated with black sludge: a mixture of EGR soot and oil vapor.
intake-manifold.where: Front side of the cylinder head.
maintenance: Cleaning recommended if the engine is fouled by EGR deposits.

egr-valve.name: EGR valve and cooler
egr-valve.description: Routes part of the exhaust gases back into the intake to lower combustion temperature and reduce nitrogen oxides (NOx). The gases first pass through a small water-cooled heat exchanger.
egr-valve.where: Left end of the cylinder head, transmission side.
maintenance: Take occasional out-of-town drives with the engine fully warm.
Clean or replace when it sticks.
faults: Clogged/stuck valve: check engine light, hesitation, black smoke, rough idle. It's the most typical fault of diesels used in the city.

exhaust-manifold.name: Exhaust manifold
exhaust-manifold.description: Cast-iron part that collects the red-hot gases from the 4 cylinders and routes them to the turbo's turbine. It operates at several hundred degrees, which is why its surface is always rusty.
exhaust-manifold.where: Rear side of the cylinder head, toward the firewall.
faults: Cracks or blown gasket: puffing/ticking when cold and exhaust smell.

dpf.name: Catalytic converter and diesel particulate filter (DPF)
dpf.description: Right after the turbo are the oxidation catalytic converter and the diesel particulate filter, which traps soot. Periodically the ECU burns it off with a "regeneration" (post-injections of diesel fuel, approx. 600 °C). Two small tubes carry the upstream and downstream pressure to a differential sensor. The Euro 6 version (K9K 628) adds a NOx trap.
dpf.where: Behind the engine, standing vertically against the firewall.
maintenance: Drives of 15–20 minutes at steady speed above 2,000 rpm help regenerations.
Use only "low SAPS" oil (ACEA C4).
faults: Clogging with city-only driving: warning light, reduced power, rising oil level (diesel fuel in the oil pan).
Faulty differential pressure sensor.

exhaust.name: Exhaust pipe and muffler
exhaust.description: Carries the gases from the DPF to the back of the car, running under the floor; the rear muffler reduces noise. On the Clio dCi the tailpipe is hidden and points downward.
exhaust.where: Under the floor pan, from the engine bay to the rear bumper.
faults: Muffler corrosion, broken rubber hangers (vibration).

battery.name: 12 V battery
battery.description: Supplies current for starting and stabilizes the electrical system. With Stop&Start a sturdier EFB battery is required. The positive terminal (+) is covered by the red cap.
battery.where: Left side of the engine bay, under a plastic cover.
maintenance: Typical life 4–6 years.
Always disconnect the negative (−) first and reconnect it last.
faults: Slow cranking, Stop&Start not engaging, random warning lights.

ecu.name: Engine control unit (ECU)
ecu.description: The computer that manages injection, turbo, EGR, DPF regeneration and glow plug preheating by reading dozens of sensors. It is connected to the OBD diagnostic port under the dashboard.
ecu.where: Next to the battery, left side.
faults: It rarely fails: more often the connectors or ground connections are corroded.

fuse-box.name: Engine bay fuse and relay box
fuse-box.description: Contains the high-current fuses and relays (fan, glow plug preheating, pump, lights). A second fuse box is inside the cabin, to the left of the steering wheel.
fuse-box.where: Left side of the engine bay, near the battery.
maintenance: Always replace a fuse with one of the same amperage (color).

starter-motor.name: Starter motor
starter-motor.description: Electric motor that turns the flywheel to start the engine. With Stop&Start it is reinforced to withstand many more starts.
starter-motor.where: Low down behind the engine, on the transmission bell housing.
faults: "Click" with no cranking (solenoid), slow cranking (brushes).

gearbox.name: JR5 manual transmission (5-speed)
gearbox.description: 5-speed manual transmission with integrated differential, operated by two cables. It is bolted to the left side of the engine; the clutch is inside the bell housing.
gearbox.where: To the left of the engine.
maintenance: Renault considers it "filled for life"; many mechanics change it around 100,000–120,000 km.
faults: Noisy bearings, stiff shifting when cold, seeping axle shaft seals.

clutch.name: Clutch and flywheel
clutch.description: Disc, pressure plate and release bearing connect and disconnect the engine and transmission when you press the pedal. It is hydraulically actuated (same fluid as the brakes).
clutch.where: Between the engine and transmission, inside the bell housing.
maintenance: Typical life 120,000–200,000 km depending on driving style.
faults: Slipping uphill in high gears, stiff pedal, judder when pulling away.

driveshafts.name: Driveshafts and CV joints
driveshafts.description: Two shafts that carry torque from the differential to the front wheels. The constant-velocity (CV) joints, protected by grease-filled rubber boots, allow the wheels to steer and follow suspension movement.
maintenance: Inspect the boots at every service.
faults: Torn boot: grease gets out, dirt gets in and the joint clicks ("tac-tac") when turning.

brake-booster.name: Brake booster and master cylinder
brake-booster.description: The brake booster (the big black "drum") uses vacuum from a vacuum pump to multiply the force of your foot; the master cylinder in front of it sends pressurized fluid to the wheels.
brake-booster.where: On the firewall, left side, in front of the driver.
faults: Hard pedal = no vacuum; spongy pedal = air in the system.

brake-fluid-reservoir.name: Brake fluid reservoir
brake-fluid-reservoir.description: Brake fluid reservoir (it also feeds the clutch hydraulics). The level drops slowly as the pads wear: a rapid drop indicates a leak.
brake-fluid-reservoir.where: At the back on the left, above the master cylinder.
maintenance: Complete flush every 2–3 years: the fluid absorbs moisture and loses effectiveness.

abs-unit.name: ABS / ESP unit
abs-unit.description: Hydraulic block with solenoid valves and a control module that modulates pressure at each wheel to prevent lock-up under braking (ABS) and correct skids (ESP). It reads the speed sensors of all 4 wheels.
faults: ABS/ESP warning lights on: often a wheel speed sensor or its wiring.

brake.front.name: Front disc brake
brake.front.description: Vented disc (rotor) that turns with the wheel, clamped by the pads mounted in the floating caliper. The front brakes do about 70% of the braking work.
maintenance: Pads: check at every service (typical life 30,000–50,000 km).
Rotors: usually every 2 pad changes.
faults: Steering wheel vibration when braking (warped rotors), squealing, dragging caliper.

brake.rear.name: Rear drum brake
brake.rear.description: On the dCi 75 the rear brakes are drums: two shoes expand against the inside of the drum. The parking brake also acts here, via a cable. The hub houses the wheel bearing with the ABS sensor ring.
maintenance: Shoes: they last a long time (often over 100,000 km); periodic cleaning and adjustment.
faults: Parking brake with long lever travel, leaking wheel cylinder.

suspension.front.name: McPherson front suspension
suspension.front.description: McPherson layout: the shock absorber with the coil spring around it also locates the wheel; at the bottom is the A-arm (lower control arm) with the ball joint. At the top, the strut mount with bearing lets the wheel steer.
maintenance: Shock absorbers: check from 80,000 km; always replace them in pairs.
Check ball joints, bushings and anti-roll bar links.
faults: Clunks over potholes (links, mounts), wallowing, uneven tire wear.
Springs broken at the last coil.

suspension.rear.name: Rear spring and shock absorber
suspension.rear.description: At the rear, the spring and shock absorber are separate and act on the torsion beam.
maintenance: Replace the shock absorbers in pairs.
faults: Oil seeping from the shock absorber, bouncing.

rear-axle.name: Rear torsion beam axle
rear-axle.description: Semi-independent axle: two trailing arms joined by a cross member that twists when one wheel rises relative to the other. A simple, robust and compact solution.
faults: Worn front axle bushings: "loose" rear end and clunks.

steering-rack.name: Steering rack and column
steering-rack.description: Rack and pinion that converts steering wheel rotation into side-to-side movement of the tie rods. Power steering is electric (motor on the column, inside the cabin): there is no power steering fluid to check.
steering-rack.where: Behind the engine, low down, bolted to the subframe.
maintenance: Have the alignment (toe) checked after impacts or when tires show abnormal wear.
faults: Play in tie rod ends and tie rods: vague steering, noises.

anti-roll-bar.name: Anti-roll bar
anti-roll-bar.description: Steel bar that connects the two front suspensions and limits body roll in corners.
faults: Worn links and bushings: "clunk-clunk" over bumps.

subframe.name: Engine subframe
subframe.description: Steel subframe bolted to the body that supports the engine/transmission (via the lower torque-reaction mount), suspension arms, steering and anti-roll bar.

wheel.name: Wheel and tire
specs: approx. 2.2–2.4 bar front / 2.0–2.2 bar rear (see the label on the driver's door)
maintenance: Check the pressure monthly with the tires cold.
Legal minimum tread depth 1.6 mm (3 mm recommended, 4 mm for winter tires).
Rotate front/rear every 10,000–15,000 km.

spare-wheel.name: Spare wheel / inflation kit
spare-wheel.description: Under the cargo floor is the compact spare (or, depending on trim, the kit with compressor and sealant) along with the jack and lug wrench.
maintenance: Check the compact spare's pressure at least once a year.
The kit's sealant has an expiration date.

hood.name: Hood
hood.description: Opens by pulling the release lever under the dashboard (left side) and then releasing the safety catch under the front edge. It is held up by a prop rod.
maintenance: Lubricate the latch and safety catch from time to time.

door.front.name: Front door
door.front.description: Door with power window, speaker and side-impact beam. The handle is body-colored.
maintenance: Lubricate the hinges and door check strap; clean the drain holes on the bottom edge.

door.rear.name: Rear door
door.rear.description: One of the Clio IV's styling touches: the handle is hidden in the black pillar next to the window, so the car looks like a 3-door. The child safety lock is on the door edge.

tailgate.name: Tailgate
tailgate.description: Gives access to the 300-liter cargo area. It is held up by two gas struts; the release button is above the license plate. It integrates the heated rear window, rear wiper, third brake light in the spoiler and the inner part of the taillights.
faults: Worn gas struts: the tailgate won't stay up.
Wiring in the rubber boot breaking (rear wiper, license plate lights).

bumper.front.name: Front bumper
bumper.front.description: Painted plastic bumper cover that integrates the grille, lower air intake, daytime running lights and license plate. Behind it are the steel bumper beam and the crash absorbers.

bumper.rear.name: Rear bumper
bumper.rear.description: Plastic rear bumper cover with reflectors and a black lower section. It can house the parking sensors.

fender.front.name: Front fender
fender.front.description: Bolt-on panel (replaceable without welding) covering the front wheel. Inside is the plastic wheel well liner.

body-shell.name: Body shell (roof, pillars, sides)
body-shell.description: Structural part of the car made of welded sheet steel: roof, pillars, rocker panels under the doors and rear quarter panels form a single piece. The low sculpted crease on the doors is the Clio IV's styling signature (design by Laurens van den Acker).

roof.name: Roof
roof.description: Sheet-steel roof panel with a short radio antenna at the rear.

grille.name: Grille and badge
grille.description: Gloss-black band joining the two headlights with the large vertical Renault diamond in the center: the "face" introduced by the Clio IV itself.

mirror.name: Side mirror
mirror.description: Power-adjustable and heated; it integrates the side turn signal.

headlight.name: Headlight
headlight.description: Halogen headlight assembly with low beam, high beam, parking light and turn signal. The bulbs are changed from behind, through the engine bay.
specs: H1 55 W (to be verified: some versions H7)
maintenance: Replace bulbs in pairs; don't touch the glass with your fingers.
Adjust headlight aim with the thumbwheel on the dashboard according to the load.

drl.name: LED daytime running lights and fog lights
drl.description: In the side air intakes of the bumper: the LED daytime running light strip (switches on automatically when the engine starts) and, below it, the fog light.

taillight.name: Taillight (outer)
taillight.description: Part of the taillight fixed to the body: tail light, brake light and turn signal.

tailgate-light.name: Taillight (on tailgate)
tailgate-light.description: Part of the taillight mounted on the tailgate: reverse light and rear fog light.

windshield.name: Windshield
windshield.description: Laminated glass bonded to the body: it adds to stiffness and acts as a backstop for the passenger airbag. At the top it houses the rain/light sensor (if equipped).
maintenance: A small chip can be repaired; if it's in the driver's field of view, the windshield must be replaced.

wipers.name: Windshield wipers
wipers.description: Two flat blades with bayonet attachment.
maintenance: Replace once a year or when they leave streaks.

washer-reservoir.name: Washer fluid reservoir
washer-reservoir.description: Top up through the blue cap. The actual reservoir is hidden low down behind the right bumper/fender.
washer-reservoir.where: Filler neck with blue cap, front right of the engine bay.
maintenance: In winter use antifreeze washer fluid, never plain water.

door-glass.front.name: Front door glass
door-glass.front.description: Tempered roll-down glass with power window regulator.

door-glass.rear.name: Rear door glass
door-glass.rear.description: Roll-down glass (power or manual depending on trim).

rear-window.name: Heated rear window
rear-window.description: Rear glass with defroster grid and rear wiper.

dashboard.name: Dashboard and interior
dashboard.description: Dashboard with central multimedia screen (7" Media Nav or R-Link), vents, climate controls and glove box. The OBD diagnostic port is low down on the driver's side.

instrument-cluster.name: Instrument cluster
instrument-cluster.description: Central digital speedometer with tachometer and fuel gauge on either side, trip computer and warning lights.
specs: glow plug preheating / injection fault if flashing

steering-wheel.name: Steering wheel and driver airbag
steering-wheel.description: Tilt and telescoping steering wheel with front airbag; the audio controls are on the satellite stalk behind the right spoke, the cruise control buttons are on the wheel.

gear-lever.name: Shift lever and parking brake
gear-lever.description: 5-speed shift lever (reverse by lifting the ring under the knob) and cable-operated mechanical parking brake.

pedals.name: Pedal assembly
pedals.description: Clutch (hydraulic), brake and electronic accelerator (potentiometer, no cable).

seat.front.name: Front seat
seat.front.description: Seat with adjustable head restraint and side airbag in the seatback; the driver's seat is height-adjustable.

seats.name: Seats
seats.description: Front seats with adjustable head restraints and side airbags in the seatbacks (the driver's seat is height-adjustable) and a three-seat rear bench with folding seatback and Isofix anchors on the outer seats.

seat.rear.name: Rear seat
seat.rear.description: Three-seat bench with folding seatback (60/40 split depending on trim) and Isofix anchors on the outer seats.

parcel-shelf.name: Cargo cover
parcel-shelf.description: Removable rigid shelf that covers the cargo area.

cabin-filter.name: Cabin air filter (pollen filter)
cabin-filter.description: Filters the air coming in through the vents. It slides out sideways from the HVAC unit, from the passenger footwell.
cabin-filter.where: Behind the dashboard, accessible low down on the passenger side.
maintenance: Replace every year or every 15,000–30,000 km: when clogged, the windows fog up and the A/C performs worse.

airbag.passenger.name: Passenger airbag
airbag.passenger.description: Front airbag on the passenger side, which can be deactivated with the key (switch on the side of the dashboard) to install a rear-facing child seat.
